title: Repair authority, portability, and critical quality failures
objective: Make the current Mez Systems baseline safe to evolve by resolving authority and deterministic-use conflicts, fixing critical accessibility and reflow defects, and releasing a self-contained portable package.

included: Authority hierarchy and reference certification states
Contradictory copy, typography, CTA, OG, blur, and Figma guidance
Focus, form, target-size, keyboard, narrow-layout, large-text, zoom, reduced-motion, and forced-colour quality
Exact assigned gradient exports and safe lockup contrast
Self-contained fonts, licences, icons, OG, email, docs, manifest, build, and clean-copy validation
excluded: Certifying the Canvas for design excellence
Resolving the final holdco mark or three candidate product cores
Starting the Taste Reverse research cycle

acceptance: One precedence path owns declarative, behavioural, and visual truth
Reference states and certification requirements are explicit
All eight pages pass eight supported widths without overflow
Navigation and FAQ keyboard contracts pass
Large-text, zoom, reduced-motion, and forced-colour checks exist
All required files and assets are inside the copied folder
A standard-library-only clean-copy validator passes without Figma or source access
Keyboard and content-stress evidence is explicit

verification.passCondition: No conflicting authority language or private portable dependency is found.
Authority, copy, tokens, contrast, assets, links, hashes, and browser evidence all pass.
A copied design-system-export validates with Python standard library only.
Eight pages at eight widths, zoom proxy, large text, navigation keyboard, and FAQ keyboard tests pass.

stopConditions: Do not promote Canvas, the website, or Figma from candidate to certified.
Do not treat the three candidate product cores as human-approved finals.
Do not invent missing assets or use approximate CSS gradients.
Stop if a clean consumer needs access outside its copied release folder.
notes: Phase 1 is a safety repair, not the strategic identity redesign scheduled for Phases 2 and 3.
